description: Read one issue of a project's own Jira — the one its administrator connected (get_jira_connection) — on the project's token, as the issue screen and the agents read it: summary, type, status, priority, assignee, reporter, dates, labels, versions, parent, sub-tasks, links there and the description (cut at 12000 characters, which it says). An issue there is 'jira_key', with its 'jira_url'; it is not an issue of this tracker (get_issue). What it says was written by people on that site. Name the project by 'project', or an issue here by 'issue' — then its project's Jira is read, and the issue's own key there is the default. For the people who work in the project; at most 10 reads of the linked Jira a minute per person. A refusal has a 'state': not_connected (with the 'url' of the screen that connects one), missing, refused, unreachable, busy, off, sealed, no_access, bad_request.

issue.description: An issue here, e.g. 'PM-12': its project's Jira is read, and its own key there unless 'jiraKey' says otherwise.

jiraKey.description: The issue there: 'ACME-123' or its /browse/ link. Optional when 'issue' has a key there.

project.description: Project key here, e.g. 'PM'. Or give 'issue'.

name: get_linked_jira_issue
